description: Local PDF text transcription for authoring review, not operational approval. Aircraft and IATA cells can span rows. Read each section in order, preserving stopline and bridge columns; no aircraft-family or variant expansion is implied.

extraction.map_label_method: Rotation-normalized CAD text; source PDF fill colors distinguish blue interior gates from black exterior stands, checked against local renders. Associations use nearest label within 35 PDF points, with visually reconciled exceptions for 162B and shared F99 at 245B/C; all require operational confirmation.
extraction.t3_asm_coordinates: Rotated for reading: x = native PDF y, source_y = negative native PDF x. Other tables retain native PDF y.
extraction.georeferencing: See georeferencing.json for the user-confirmed pin anchor, physical-pixel scale, vector frame matches, overview frame picks, held-out registration checks and accuracy limitations. These update label positions only, not operational permissions.
extraction.asm_cell_method: Painted horizontal PDF vector grid lines spanning the interiors of aircraft, comment/bridge and stopline columns; clipping boxes and short underlines excluded, stroke edges clustered within 1 PDF point. Native PDF y for T1/IFC; negative native PDF x for T3. Cell intervals distinguish wrapped aircraft names and merged operating requirements; no revision-history pages included.

Note 1.— Special Operating Procedure for Bridge Manoeuvring Clearances < 1.5m
 There must be a second person on the apron level maintaining eye contact or voice contact (via radio, telephone, etc.) with the bridge operator ensuring
proper clearance with the aircraft is maintained.
 When the bridge is within the 0.75m – 1.49m zone, the bridge operator must move the bridge using the lowest operating speed.
 These same conditions apply upon removal of the bridge from the aircraft.
Note 2. – PBB Spotter Requirements for all dual bridge stands
‡ When either B1 or B2 (or both) are used:
 A ground spotter is used to ensure adequate clearance between bridges
 The bridge operator maintains visual contact with the spotter throughout the maneuvering process
General Note
The bridge parking circle represents the safe zone between the bridge and the aircraft. When the wheels of the bridge are parked within the bridge parking circle and an
aircraft is parked on the correct stopline, a safe distance between the bridge and the aircraft will always be maintained.
